_meta.notes: The state with no control, which is the half a happy-path render never shows. Every tooling this vehicle needs is already owned, so there is nothing to buy and no button is drawn: the command's only answer here is a refusal, and a control whose sole outcome is a refusal is a control that should not be on screen. The cards remain, because an owned tooling is a real reading and says the money has already been spent, rather than leaving an operator to infer it from an absence. Note also what is NOT on these cards: no price and no standing charge. RP-1 reports a tooled part's surcharge as a zero rather than as absent, and a zero drawn beside the words per build is a bill for nothing. This is deliberately NOT the same picture as the channel saying nothing at all, which renders no section whatsoever: no sample means no ship on the editor's table or RP-1's tooling switched off, and neither of those is a finished vehicle. Scoped to the AUGMENT, so the section is photographed on its own terms rather than inside a host whose balances are the subject of the other scene.
_meta.notes2: No career record is emitted, and it is not an omission: this section draws no balance of its own. The funds and the unlock credit belong to the host, once, and the widget-scoped scene beside this is where they are shown.

_scene.caption: Every tooling on this vehicle is already owned: the cards say so and no purchase control is offered, because there is nothing left to buy

emits.comment: The craft listing, empty. Naming an augment mounts the whole rp1-vehicle-assembly.sections slot, so the START A BUILD section draws in this scene too and without this it photographed "Waiting for the craft listing" under two fully described toolings. An empty list is the honest answer for a career with nothing saved, and it is a different sentence from a listing that has not arrived.
